stem: What makes growth assessment most useful in follow-up for a school-aged child with recurrent abdominal symptoms?

options.text: Using serial measurements plotted over time
Relying on the most recent measurement only
Avoiding growth charts to reduce measurement variation
Assessing height alone because weight fluctuates
Repeating blood tests before considering anthropometry

explanation: Serial measurements plotted over time are the most useful way to assess growth in follow-up because they show trends rather than a single isolated value.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Page 12

optionExplanations.A: Correct because serial measurements plotted over time allow growth trends to be assessed more accurately than a single measurement.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because a single recent value does not show growth trend or progression over time.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because growth charts are used to improve, not reduce, the value of growth assessment.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because both height and weight contribute to growth assessment, and height alone is incomplete.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because anthropometric assessment should not be delayed until blood tests are repeated.
